outcome: A project can push, open a pull request, and merge on GitHub, Gitea, or GitLab through the same WorkItem records, while local Git still works without GitHub and hosted credentials are never persisted
acceptance: a project can register a GitHub, Gitea, or GitLab repository on the same WorkItem records as local Git
local Git still works without GitHub
unknown provider or missing hosted remote metadata fails loud
hosted push, open pull request, and merge remain separate actions
hosted push, open pull request, and merge still require human approval
hosted credentials are supplied at call time or from the environment and are never persisted
GitHub, Gitea, and GitLab use provider-specific pull-request and merge endpoints
Code View shows the hosted pull-request URL
customers cannot register hosted repositories or push
inScope: hosted GitHub, Gitea, and GitLab write adapters
shared WorkItem branch and pull-request records
assumptions: local Git repository, branch, changeset, and pull-request records already exist
C1 authority remains the push, pull-request, and merge gate
